doc.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Ordering records versus the MP3 era
summary: Waiting for the Buddy Rich records and cherishing them, versus too much information now.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah, it’s easy to sound like these aren’t the good old days. We had the good old days. But I think the process of going to a record store and hearing something on the radio and seeking it out and buying a physical product, at least for our generation, worked for us.

Yes. I remember getting my first teacher had the Buddy Rich Swinging You Big Band, which I’m sure you have. And I ordered it. I had to go to the store and order it because they didn’t have it. And then I got the Swinging Big Face?

But I had to order it you know. The guy would look it up in this big fat catalogue and get the number and I had to wait a couple of weeks to get it you know. But then you got that record and you cherished it.

And you heard it for the next five years almost every day. So I think those days are gone, because now we’ve got too much information and you can not even listen to all that information. You don’t have enough time.
